'''Janina Maultzsch''' is a German physicist who is the Chair of [[Experimental Physics]] at [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|Friedrich-Alexander-Universität]] Erlangen-Nürnberg. Her research considers the electronic and optical properties of carbon [[nanomaterials]]. 

== Early life and education ==
Maultzsch was an undergraduate student at [[Technische Universität Berlin]], where she studied physics.{{cn|date=July 2022}} She remained in Berlin for doctoral research, investigating the vibrational properties of [[carbon allotropes]] including [[nanotubes]] and [[graphite]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Vibrational properties of carbon nanotubes and graphite |date=2004 |language=English |first=Janina |last=Maultzsch|oclc=916652128 }}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Maultzsch moved to the [[University of Siegen]], where she worked on [[Near-field scanning optical microscope|near field microscopy]].{{cn|date=July 2022}} She returned to Technische Universität Berlin in late 2004, where she worked as a researcher in the Institute of Solid State Physics. She moved to [[Columbia University]] in 2006, working as a postdoctoral researcher with [[Tony Heinz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plenary Speakers |url=https://www.mrs.org/icors/speakers/plenary-speakers |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=www.mrs.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chemistry Group Directory |url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/chemistry/fac-bios/brus/group/pages/pubs.html |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=www.columbia.edu}}</ref> She returned Technische Universität Berlin in 2008, where she was made an assistant professor. She is interested in low-dimensional materials, including [[transition-metal dichalcogenide]]s and [[graphene]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Janina Maultzsch › Lehrstuhl f. Experimentalphysik |date=19 April 2017 |url=https://www.exphys.nat.fau.de/person/janina-maultzsch/ |access-date=2022-07-03 |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Guest Lecture Prof. Janina Maultzsch |url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/chemie/sfb1415/der-sfb/news/gastvortrag-prof-janina-maultzsch?set_language=en |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=TU Dresden |language=en}}</ref>

Maultzsch contributed to the understanding of [[carbon nanotubes]]. In particular, she investigated their electronic and vibrational properties.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=Reich |first1=Stephanie |title=Carbon nanotubes: basic concepts and physical properties |last2=Maultzsch |first2=Janina |date=2004 |publisher=Wiley-VCH |others=C. Thomsen, J. Maultzsch |isbn=3-527-40386-8 |location=Weinheim |oclc=50434660 |author-link=Stephanie Reich}}</ref> She made use of resonant [[Raman spectroscopy]] to uncover the optical transition energies and radial mode frequencies of various metallic and semiconducting nanotubes. She showed that the optical transition energies and electronic structures depend on the [[chirality (physics)|chirality]] index of the nanotube. She revealed that electron-phonon coupling increases for smaller chiral angles.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Telg |first1=H. |last2=Maultzsch |first2=J. |last3=Reich |first3=S. |last4=Hennrich |first4=F. |last5=Thomsen |first5=C. |date=2004-10-18 |title=Chirality Distribution and Transition Energies of Carbon Nanotubes |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.177401 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=93 |issue=17 |article-number=177401 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.177401|pmid=15525124 |arxiv=cond-mat/0409220 |bibcode=2004PhRvL..93q7401T |s2cid=27782361 }}</ref>

In 2010, Maultzsch was awarded an [[ERC Starting Grant]] focused on the characterisation of carbon nanomaterials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TU Berlin erhält drei der renommierten "ERC Starting Grants" |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news379182 |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=idw-online.de}}</ref> In 2015, she was promoted to full Professor for Novel Materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Janina Maultzsch – CV › Lehrstuhl f. Experimentalphysik |url=https://www.exphys.nat.fau.de/team/prof-janina-maultzsch-cv/ |access-date=2022-07-03 |language=de-DE}}</ref> In 2017, Maultzsch was appointed the Chair of Experimental Physics at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Janina Maultzsch › Lehrstuhl f. Experimentalphysik |date=19 April 2017 |url=https://www.exphys.nat.fau.de/person/janina-maultzsch/ |access-date=2022-07-03 |language=de-DE}}</ref>
